name: Norms, identity, hierarchy, and order transition
derived_requirement: The architecture must represent normative restraint, identity, status hierarchy, and the international order that nuclear possession helps constitute.
mechanism: Actors may pursue or reject weapons because of identity and legitimacy rather than a fungible material payoff; supplier-control regimes may reproduce the hierarchy that creates resistance.
current_gap: Status and legitimacy are secondary scalar incentives, and the end state lacks an order-transition theory.
required_change: Add independent norm, identity, hierarchy, and legitimacy states; model norm internalization and backlash; test equal-governance reforms against enforcement efficacy.
acceptance_test: The model distinguishes materially similar cases with divergent restraint caused by identity or norms and reproduces legitimacy backlash under asymmetric governance.

name: Emerging technology and evidence integrity
derived_requirement: Every breakout and response clock must be conditioned on changing sensing, cyber, AI, space, precision-strike, delivery, and survivability capabilities.
mechanism: Technology can accelerate detection and response while also corrupting evidence, compressing decisions, exposing forces, and increasing preemption or automation risk.
current_gap: The model assumes intact evidence, annual technology movement, and no cross-domain operational coupling.
required_change: Add cyber-integrity states, correlated sensor failure, adversarial data manipulation, delivery and survivability stages, and technology distributions with competing effects.
acceptance_test: The architecture remains fail-safe under compromised telemetry, AI disagreement, space loss, false targeting confidence, and a shortened coercive-advantage clock.

name: Regional posture and decision lineage
derived_requirement: Threat objects and security substitutions must preserve regional doctrine, posture, alliance structure, domestic coalition, and the lineage of prior bargains and failures.
mechanism: The same technical capability has different meaning under recessed deterrence, ready arsenals, sanctuary, alliance protection, regime-security strategies, and failed agreements.
current_gap: Actors are stylized global archetypes with weak regional network and historical-memory representation.
required_change: Replace global coverage percentages with regional security graphs, posture states, decision-history memory, and actor-specific doctrine.
acceptance_test: The system differentiates the causal and operational pathways of Europe, the Korean Peninsula, South Asia, the Middle East, and other selected systems without manual outcome forcing.

name: Reversal pathways, relapse, and post-bargain security
derived_requirement: Rollback must branch by causal pathway and preserve relapse risk after apparent closure.
mechanism: Voluntary renunciation, negotiated rollback, inherited-arsenal transfer, military defeat, and coerced dismantlement produce different assurance, monitoring, identity, and relapse dynamics.
current_gap: Rollback is a generic cooperative transition with insufficient post-deal political and security memory.
required_change: Add reversal types, post-bargain security outcomes, assurance credibility, identity conversion, monitoring persistence, and relapse hazards.
acceptance_test: Historical replay distinguishes South Africa, Kazakhstan, Ukraine, Libya, Iraq, Iran, North Korea, and other cases using pre-specified variables.

name: Marginal value over the existing regime and asymmetry tradeoff
derived_requirement: Breakout Parity must demonstrate which outcomes improve beyond the existing nonproliferation regime and what is lost when legal hierarchy is reduced.
mechanism: Current restraint may depend partly on differentiated power, hegemonic leadership, norms, and existing institutions; symmetry can improve legitimacy while weakening enforcement arrangements.
current_gap: The baseline treats current institutions as comparatively inert and assumes fairness monotonically increases stability.
required_change: Model the existing regime as an active causal system and run marginal component comparisons, including the legitimacy-enforcement tradeoff.
acceptance_test: Each proposed component shows incremental value, substitution, or a documented negative interaction against a calibrated existing-regime baseline.

name: Model epistemics and external validity
derived_requirement: Simulation and tabletop outputs must carry explicit epistemic labels and cannot be converted into frequencies or forecasts without empirical validation.
mechanism: Model structure, assumptions, participant incentives, scenario design, and analyst interpretation can dominate apparent results.
current_gap: Regime probabilities are visually precise despite stylized actors, assumptions, and no external-validity programme.
required_change: Use model ensembles, pre-registration, sensitivity and calibration dashboards, historical replay, red-team replication, and an explicit forecast prohibition.
acceptance_test: Independent teams reproduce the qualitative mechanism findings across alternative model structures and identify where conclusions reverse.
